diagnostic_evidence.quote: defining $\alpha = -\frac{1}{\|\b\|_2}(\B_k)_{1,1}(\v_{\min})_1 $, the MINBERR-NE solution after $k$ iterations satisfies \x_k :=\!\argmin_{\x\in \mathrm{Span}(\Q_k)}\!\!\berr_{\A,\b}(\x) \ = \ \frac1\alpha\Q_k\v_{\min},\qquad \berr_{\A,\b}(\x_k) = \sigma_{\min}.

Moreover, for any $\widehat\v\in\mathbb{R}^{k}$, defining $\widehat\alpha=-\frac{1}{\|\b\|_2}\left((\T_k)_{1,1}(\widehat\v)_1 +(\T_k)_{1,2}(\widehat\v)_2\right)$ and $\widehat\x = \frac1\alpha\Q_k\widehat\v,$ we have $\berr_{\A,\b}(\widehat\x) = \|\tilde \T_k\widehat\v\|_2/\|\widehat \v\|_2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The first row of the GEP (eq:minberrGEP) reads ||b||_2^2 - b^T A Q_k y = 0, i.e. (T_k)_{1,1} y_1 + (T_k)_{1,2} y_2 = ||b||_2; substituting y = v_min/alpha therefore forces alpha = +((T_k)_{1,1}(v_min)_1 + (T_k)_{1,2}(v_min)_2)/||b||_2, the opposite of the stated sign (equivalently, W[0; v_min] = [alpha; v_min] is parallel to [-1; y] only with y = -v_min/alpha). With the stated sign the returned iterate is the negative of the true MINBERR solution: e.g. A = diag(2,1), b = (1,1)^T, k = 1 gives alpha_1 = 3/2, beta_2 = 1/2, T~_1 = [1/2], v_min = [1], alpha = -(3/2)/sqrt(2), x_k = (1/alpha) q_1 = (-2/3,-2/3) with berr = ||A x_k - b||_2/(2||x_k||_2) = sqrt(74)/(4 sqrt(2)) ~ 1.52, while the true minimizer (2/3,2/3) has berr = 1/4. The same wrong sign appears in Proposition prop:minberrNE and in the final steps of Algorithms alg:MINBERR and alg:MINBERRnonsym. The supporting deflation is also false as stated: with w_1 = (1/||b||)[1,-(T_k)_{1,1},-(T_k)_{1,2},0,...,0], the first row of W^T M is [1,(T_k)_{1,1}/||b||,(T_k)_{1,2}/||b||,0,...,0], not [1,0,...,0], so eq:pairs does not hold; the correct W has the full first row of M^{-1} (all entries generally nonzero).

failure_location.quote: the smallest eigenpair of the generalized eigenvalue problem~\eqref{eq:MM} is given by $(\sigma_{\min}^2,\frac1\alpha\v_{\min})$, where $\alpha =-\frac{1}{\|\b\|_2}\left((\T_k)_{1,1}(\v_{\min})_1 +(\T_k)_{1,2}(\v_{\min})_2\right)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of alpha in Lemma l:quotient and Proposition prop:minberrNE (equivalently define the eigenvector component as y = -v_min/alpha), propagate the correction to the final steps of Algorithms alg:MINBERR and alg:MINBERRnonsym, and repair the deflation by taking W's first row to be the full first row of M^{-1}, or by directly verifying that [-1; v_min/alpha] with alpha = ((T_k)_{1,1}(v_min)_1+(T_k)_{1,2}(v_min)_2)/||b||_2 solves the GEP via its first-row constraint. All rates and guarantees then stand.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma l:quotient's eigenpair and solution formula are false as stated, and its proof's congruence (eq:pairs) does not hold for the given W. Algorithms alg:MINBERR and alg:MINBERRnonsym consequently return the negative of the true (near-)minimizer, so their Ensure contracts (berr < epsilon) and the guarantees of thm:minberrcost (berr(x_k) <= 1.5 min) and c:minberr fail for the procedures as written; prop:minberrNE carries the same sign error. The convergence rates of t:minberr itself are unaffected (they concern the exact minimizer).
issues.title: Sign error in the MINBERR/MINBERR-NE eigenvector formula (alpha) and false deflation congruence
issues.why_classification: The procedures return the negative of the true minimizer, so their output contracts and the dependent guarantees fail as written; the repair (sign flip plus a replacement of the false deflation congruence, a contained new argument) preserves every rate and guarantee, but it is more than a typo fix because the stated congruence is false and a replacement argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The smallest eigenvalue $\lambda_{\min}$, which is nonnegative, is equal to the square of the backward error of the MINBERR solution, that is, $\lambda_{\min} = (\berr_{\A,\b}(\x_k))^2$.

Attempt Cholesky factorization of $\tilde \G-\epsilon^2 \I_k = \bf{R}^\top \bf{R}$ (by computing the three nonzero entries in $\bf{R}$'s last column); if this breaks down (i.e., $\sigma_{\min}(\tilde\T_k)=\berr_{\A,\b}(x_k)<\epsilon$), proceed to step 7.
If $d>0$, return to step 2. Else, $\sigma_{\min}(\tilde \B_k)=\berr_{\A,\b}(x_k)<\epsilon,$ so go to step 7.

issues.failure_explanation: The GEP value is lambda_min = min_y ||A Q_k y - b||_2^2/||y||_2^2 = ||A||_2^2 (min berr)^2, because berr(x) = ||Ax-b||_2/(||A||_2 ||x||_2) while the quotient in eq:GRQ has no ||A||_2 normalization; hence the correct identities are lambda_min = ||A||_2^2 berr(x_k)^2 and berr(x_k) = sigma_min(T~_k)/||A||_2 (similarly berr(x_hat) = ||T~_k v_hat||_2/(||A||_2||v_hat||_2), and the MINBERR-NE analogs with B~_k). Counterexample: A = diag(2,1), b = (1,1)^T, k = 1 has sigma_min(T~_1) = 1/2 but berr(x_k) = 1/4 = sigma_min/||A||_2. Consequently the stopping tests in the algorithms (Cholesky of G~ - epsilon^2 I in alg:MINBERR; dqds shift epsilon in alg:MINBERRnonsym) trigger only when berr < epsilon/||A||_2, so the procedures need O(sqrt(||A||_2/epsilon)) iterations rather than the advertised O(1/sqrt(epsilon)), and the complexity in c:minberr is not achieved as written (the Ensure contracts still hold since epsilon/||A||_2 < epsilon).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the identities to berr(x_k) = sigma_min(T~_k)/||A||_2 and lambda_min = ||A||_2^2 (berr(x_k))^2 (and the analogous statements in prop:minberrNE), and rescale the stopping tests: Cholesky of G~ - epsilon^2 ||A||_2^2 I in alg:MINBERR and dqds shift epsilon ||A||_2 in alg:MINBERRnonsym. These are one-line changes that restore every claim.
issues.overall_effect: The identities berr(x_k) = sigma_min(T~_k), lambda_min = (berr(x_k))^2 and berr(x_hat) = ||T~_k v_hat||_2/||v_hat||_2 (and the MINBERR-NE analogs) are false by a factor ||A||_2; the convergence tests in both algorithms are conservative by the same factor, inflating the iteration count by sqrt(||A||_2), so the stated O((1/sqrt(epsilon))(T_A+n+log(1/delta))) complexity of c:minberr is not achieved by the procedures as written. thm:minberrcost's relative guarantee survives because the factor cancels between sigma_min and the true minimum.
issues.title: Missing 1/||A||_2 factor in the berr = sigma_min identities; stopping tests miscalibrated by ||A||_2
issues.why_classification: The false identities and miscalibrated tests are repaired by a one-line rescaling that preserves every substantive claim and guarantee; the procedures are conservative (the Ensure contracts still hold) and no mathematical content is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound cited from trefbau is the standard MINRES estimate in the 2-norm, i.e. it certifies Lemma l:forward with M = I (alpha = 0); it does not provide an M = Ã^2-norm (alpha = 1) error bound, so the hypothesis of Lemma l:forward is not established for MINRES as written. Using M = I gives berr <= epsilon/(1-epsilon) and the same final bound 5(log k/k)^2, so the theorem's conclusion is unaffected.

failure_location.quote: where we use $\M=\tilde\A^2$ for MINRES and $\M=\tilde\A$ for CG.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'M = Ã^2 for MINRES' with the 2-norm guarantee (M = I, i.e. alpha = 0 in Lemma l:forward); the rest of the proof is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the proof of t:perturbed-minres is affected: as written it invokes Lemma l:forward with a norm that the MINRES guarantee does not certify. The theorem's statement and conclusion remain correct once M = I is used for MINRES.
issues.title: MINRES error norm misidentified as M = Ã^2 in the regularized CG/MINRES proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem's conclusion is correct; only the proof misidentifies the norm. The one-line correction leaves the argument and all guarantees intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $\ell\geq \frac{1}{2} \Big[ 1 + \frac{\ln\left( \frac{32n \ln(2/\delta)}{\pi \delta^2 \Delta} \right)}{\ln(1 + \Delta/2)} \Big]$ for $\Delta\in(0,1)$, then with probability $1-\delta$ we have ${\bf v}_{\ell}^\top \M {\bf v}_{\ell}/\|{\bf v}_{\ell}\|_2^2\leq (1+\Delta)\lambda_{\min}$.
In particular, for a $1/2$-relative error ($\Delta = 0.5$), we require $\ell \geq 2.23 \ln(n/\delta^2)$.
$\sum c_j^2$ follows $\chi^2_{|S_{\mathrm{high}}|}$, so by~\cite[Eqn.~(4.3)]{laurent2000adaptive} we see that with probability $1-\delta/2$, we have $\sum c_j^2 \leq n \ln(2/\delta)$.

issues.failure_explanation: At n = k and Delta = 1/2 the hypothesis of Lemma lemma:invit is ell >= (1/2)[1 + ln(64 k ln(2/delta)/(pi delta^2))/ln(5/4)] ~= 2.2406 ln(k/delta^2) + O(ln ln(2/delta)), which exceeds the 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) used in the algorithms and in the proof of thm:minberrcost; the appendix's summary 'ell >= 2.23 ln(n/delta^2)' is inconsistent with its own derived formula. Moreover the chi^2 tail bound 'sum c_j^2 <= n ln(2/delta) with probability 1-delta/2' does not hold for all n, delta (it fails, e.g., for small n when delta = 1/2). Hence the claimed 1.5-relative-error Rayleigh-quotient guarantee with probability 1-delta does not follow as stated.

failure_location.quote: Applying Lemma \ref{lemma:invit} to $\tilde \T^\top\tilde \T$ shows that $\ell \geq 2.23 \ln(k / \delta^2)$ steps of inverse iteration suffice to get $\Delta=1/2$ relative accuracy with probability at least $1-\delta$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Increase the inverse-iteration count in Algorithms alg:MINBERR and alg:MINBERRnonsym and in thm:minberrcost (e.g. ell = 3 ln(k/delta^2), absorbed in log(1/delta)) and repair the chi^2 tail-bound application (restrict to the regime where it holds or use a bound valid for all n, delta).
issues.overall_effect: thm:minberrcost's assertion that 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) inverse iterations suffice for a (1+1/2)-relative-error Rayleigh quotient with probability 1-delta is unsupported by its own cited lemma, and c:minberr's 'with probability at least 1-delta' inherits the gap. Rates and complexity are otherwise unaffected.
issues.title: Inverse-iteration count 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) violates Lemma lemma:invit's hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Only a quantitative constant in a subroutine guarantee is affected; bumping the iteration count and fixing the tail bound restores the claim with no change to rates or complexity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Specifically, our experiments suggest that for any sufficiently large $k$ and $\kappa$, we can find a problem instance for which the backward error of \algne\ after $k$ iterations is at least $\min\{1, \log_{10}(\kappa)/k\}$.
We extend this approach via normal equations to solving general linear systems, for which we empirically observe $O(1/k)$ convergence.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction asserts as an established construction that MINBERR-NE incurs backward error at least log(kappa(A))/k after k iterations on a family of hard instances, but the paper contains no theorem proving this; the experiments section states only that experiments suggest the bound (min{1, log10(kappa)/k}), and the abstract carefully says 'we empirically observe O(1/k) convergence'. The intro thus presents an empirical observation as a proven result.

failure_location.quote: However, we are able to construct a family of hard problem instances for which the \algne\ backward error is at least $\log(\kappa(\A))/k$ after $k$ iterations, suggesting that no deterministic Krylov method can attain truly universal convergence for general systems.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Hedge the sentence as an empirical observation (matching the abstract and the experiments section) or supply a theorem with proof.
issues.overall_effect: A prose overclaim about what the paper establishes: readers of the introduction may mistake an empirically suggested lower bound for a theorem. No formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: Introduction overclaims the MINBERR-NE hard-instance lower bound as a construction; it is only empirical
issues.why_classification: The discrepancy is in the presentation of the evidence only; the body of the paper is appropriately hedged, and no formal claim needs to be withdrawn.
